title: World Cinema Radar — the podcast, Friday 6 November 2026

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hello, and welcome to World Cinema Radar, the podcast. I'm {A}, and today is Friday the sixth of November, twenty twenty-six.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And I'm {B}. <chuckle> Friday, so cinemas are full of new things. Let's see what the Radar found this morning.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We have three big topics. First, a long, faithful version of Les Misérables that opens in Spain today.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Second, a small Catalan horror film from two cousins, which played at Sitges. I'm quite curious about that one.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And third, a festival that starts today far away from here: Tallinn Black Nights, in Estonia. Thirty years old, and huge.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Plus a Belgian opera tonight, the platforms, and the calendar for the next three weeks. As always, the full edition is in the app.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good. And one reminder: we haven't seen these films. When we talk about a review, it is somebody else's opinion, and we'll say whose.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A quick note about how we work. Everything we say comes from the written edition of today, with its sources, and nothing from memory.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes, and when a fact is only in one guide, we say so. That happens today with the platform list.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's a gentle Friday for news, but a rich one for things to watch. So let's not waste time.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. Let's start with Fred Cavayé.

segments.title: Les Misérables, eleven and a documentary

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, Les Misérables. In Spain it's Los miserables, and it opens today. Directed by Fred Cavayé, with Vincent Lindon as Jean Valjean.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And Tahar Rahim as Javert. That's a great pairing on paper. <breath> Add Camille Cottin, Benjamin Lavernhe and Noémie Merlant.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Wow, that is a serious cast. How long is it? Because I know Hugo is not a short novel.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Cinemascomics says close to three hours. So, bring a snack.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: <chuckle> Fair. It was shown in San Sebastián, and SensaCine's critic wrote about it there. What did she think?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: She liked the fidelity. She says it translates Hugo's novel precisely, the period world is well built, and Lindon and Rahim are very good.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: |oh nice| But?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: But she says that the same fidelity is the limit. The film doesn't find a new way to tell the story, and for her the second half feels heavy.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, a respectable, classical adaptation. Which is not an insult, honestly. Some days that is exactly what you want.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Exactly. For someone who likes period cinema, it's a safe bet. Our affinity note is three out of five, medium confidence.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And again, that's the critic's view. We haven't seen it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. Now, the one I'm more excited about. A film simply called eleven.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Just the number. <giggle> Love it. What's the story?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's the first feature by Paula and Clàudia Serra. They're cousins, both born in nineteen ninety-eight, a month apart.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A month apart! And they started it as a class script at Pompeu Fabra University, according to Ara.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. And then producer David Matamoros helped turn it into a real production. At Sitges it was the only film in original Catalan in the competition.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's a nice detail. So what happens, without spoilers?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A group of scouts, two leaders and ten children, goes up the mountain. A snowstorm cuts them off in a refuge, and then an unexpected figure appears.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Oh, I like that. Mistrust in a closed place, in the snow.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The directors say they weren't so interested in where the evil comes from. They were interested in the argument it creates among the adults when it has the face of a child.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: |hmm| That's much more interesting than a monster. It runs about ninety minutes, which is perfect for this kind of story.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And Ara singles out Mia Sala-Patau, who plays one of the leaders. Our note for eleven is four out of five, but low confidence, because we have only read an interview and synopses.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Honestly? Of the two, this is the one I'd go and see first. <chuckle>

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Of course you would. There's also a documentary today: Por qué no escribo nada, by Isabel Fernández.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: About the novelist Carmen Laforet. With contributions from Najat El Hachmi and Laura Freixas, and it won best music at the BCN Film Fest.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let me go back to the Hugo for a second. The story is the one everybody knows: a man steals bread, and a policeman chases him for decades.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And that is the beauty of it. You know the shape, so the question is only what the film does with it. The critic's answer is: nothing very new, but it does it carefully.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: There is also the length. Three hours in a cinema is a commitment. <breath> But with this kind of material, a shorter version usually loses the minor characters.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The critic mentions them, by the way: the supporting characters and the young rebels all get their place. So at least it doesn't rush.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Okay, but is that a plus for you? Be honest.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Honestly? It depends on the evening. If I want a big, old-fashioned story with good actors, yes. If I want to be surprised, then I'd pick eleven. <laugh>

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: You always pick the horror one. It's in the profile, though. Terror in all its variants, and a Catalan mountain story fits very well.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One more thing about eleven. Paula Serra says horror films scared them a lot before they made it, and they watched many while preparing it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: |really?| Yes. And it wasn't even meant to be horror at the beginning. It started as a story about scouts who find another child.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I like that. The genre arrives because the story demands it, not the other way around.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the Sitges detail again: they had never been to the festival before. Their first feature, and straight into the competition.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's a good way to start a career. We'll see if the film is as good as the idea.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Nice. And the rest of today's openings, Godzilla, Sacamantecas, Ruega por nosotras, they were in the earlier editions, so we won't repeat them.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now, a festival. Tallinn Black Nights, called PÖFF, starts today, and it runs until the twenty-second of November.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Thirtieth edition. And the numbers are big: two hundred and thirty features and two hundred and fifty-nine shorts, from eighty-seven countries.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A hundred and seven world premieres, says the festival's own programme. That's a lot of films nobody has seen yet.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The opening film is Ulya, a co-production between Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, led by Latvia.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And the names in the programme are interesting. Andrey Zvyagintsev has a film called Minotaur.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Martin McDonagh has Wild Horse Nine. <short pause> I would love to know what that one is.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Paweł Pawlikowski has Fatherland, Peter Farrelly has I Am Rocky, and there's The Black Ball, by Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's the Spanish duo, no? Interesting to see them in the Baltics.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The page doesn't say what country it represents, so we just say who directs it. There's also a spotlight on Basque cinema.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good for Basque cinema. And there's a film about the architect Louis Kahn, Joy Will Prevail, with its international premiere tomorrow.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes, Saturday the seventh. The director, Max Korman, and the actor Griffin Dunne will hold an open press conference.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The competitions are staged in turns. The documentary ones run from the seventh to the thirteenth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And then the Official Selection, First Feature, Critics' Picks and the others, from the thirteenth to the nineteenth.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Important to say: the pages we read don't list the jury or the full competition, so we don't invent them.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let me give a bit of context. This is the thirtieth edition, so the festival is celebrating.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: They even made a special stamp and decorated a tram with artwork by the animator Priit Pärn. I love that.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A tram! <giggle> A festival you can ride.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: There are also three exhibitions opened for the anniversary, and the industry side, Industry at Tallinn, runs from the ninth to the twentieth of November.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And tickets are cheap. Thirteen euros for the main programme, eleven for the shorts and Just Film.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: For anyone who loves discoveries, that is the thing. A hundred and seven world premieres, so many names will be new.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And it fits the minor cinemas side of the profile. Baltic films, Basque cinema, debut features. Far from the Hollywood noise.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Still, we have to be careful. A name in a programme is only a name. We don't know what these films are like, or whether any will be released in Spain.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: True. We'll follow the awards at the end of the festival and tell you.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And we don't know which of these will reach Spain. But festival news is like that. You hear the names first, then you wait.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let's go to the platforms. A guide from MarketingDirecto lists what arrives in Spain from today until the fifteenth.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: On Netflix today: a film called Un amor posible, the series Palacio, and a documentary, Desprotexida: El crimen de Pazos.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: On Movistar Plus there's Cumbres borrascosas, which is Wuthering Heights, and the third season of a documentary series about photographs.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Prime Video has Campus Drivers, and HBO Max has a series called Melania Rea.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And Filmin has five. We covered Duse and Barrio Triste yesterday, but the list also has Broken English and En la alcoba del sultán.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Later: Carmen Curlers, season three, on Filmin on the tenth. And La copia perfecta on the thirteenth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One warning: it's a single guide, so dates can move. Check the platform before you plan your weekend.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Something I noticed in that guide: it's a very Movistar weekend. After Wuthering Heights today, the seventh brings two more films, the eighth and the ninth too.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It looks like a film every day. Zona cero, 9 lunas, Hermanos. We know the titles, not much more, so we won't pretend.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. And on the twelfth HBO Max puts a few classics in the catalogue, like 1917 and Little Miss Sunshine.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Nice for a rewatch. And on the thirteenth, Netflix has Heartland and a miniseries about the Pazos crime.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: There's also a Netflix documentary about the photographer Avedon on the eleventh, if you like photography.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Always. <chuckle> Okay. Now the opera.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Tonight at seven in the evening, Central European time, OperaVision lists De Materie, by Louis Andriessen.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The Dutch composer. It comes from Opera Ballet Vlaanderen, in Belgium.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The company says it's a new production, directed by Phia Ménard, conducted by Bas Wiegers, about an hour and fifty minutes.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: An hour and fifty. That's not too long for a Friday night.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: <chuckle> But careful. The OperaVision page doesn't tell us the subtitles, or how long it stays online. So we don't call it a complete recording with access; it's a scheduled broadcast.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Fine. And there's more coming in the same list: Šárka by Janáček on the fifteenth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Two things on the twenty-second, a children's piece called Little Bear and the Ice Mountain, and a Turandot set in a museum.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And Britten's Peter Grimes, from the Finnish National Opera, on the twenty-sixth. Mark that one.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A word on the composer. Louis Andriessen was Dutch, and De Materie is the title of this piece. It is a contemporary work.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I have only heard the name. So not a traditional opera?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I'd better not say too much, because all I can verify is what the company and OperaVision say. The company's page says the production is directed by Phia Ménard, so it's a new view of the piece.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Fair enough. And that is the point of the stage section every day: we look for full recordings you can really watch from Spain, with clear access.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Today we found a scheduled broadcast, not a complete recording with a stated window. So we tell you, and we link the sources.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which is better than guessing. <chuckle>

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And Le Roi d'Ys is still marked last chance to watch. We mentioned it before.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Calendar time. Friday the sixth is today: Tallinn opens, De Materie tonight, and the platform releases.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Saturday the seventh, Joy Will Prevail premieres in Tallinn. Sunday the eighth, City of God season two arrives on HBO Max in Spain.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Tuesday the tenth, the Royal Ballet and Opera's Carmen is in cinemas, but Spain is not confirmed.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Wednesday the eleventh, El cuerpo and Avedon on Netflix. Friday the thirteenth, La copia perfecta on Filmin.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then the fifteenth, Šárka. The twenty-second, Tallinn closes. And the twenty-sixth, Peter Grimes.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let me read the weekend again for people who are planning. Friday: Tallinn, De Materie and the Spanish premieres.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Saturday: Kahn's film in Tallinn, and the documentary competitions going on. Sunday: City of God on HBO Max.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And next week is quieter in cinemas for us: Carmen on Tuesday, then Netflix on Wednesday.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The calendar has all of it, with the territory for each date. That matters, because a date in Estonia is not a date in Spain.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One more detail for the week after. On the twelfth there are classics on HBO Max, and on the thirteenth the second Filmin title I mentioned.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And the twenty-second is a busy day: Tallinn closes, and OperaVision lists two titles that afternoon.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Dates come from the guides and may change, as always.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Picks time. Les Misérables first. Affinity three out of five, medium confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A period drama with a strong cast, but the critic we cited warns about a heavy second half. If you love Hugo, go.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Eleven. Four out of five, low confidence. Mountain horror, snow, mistrust, and two debut directors. My personal pick.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And Joy Will Prevail, from Tallinn. Three out of five, low confidence, because all we know is the subject: Louis Kahn. And it has no date in Spain.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A reminder that these numbers are our editorial affinity. They are not a critics' score or an audience score.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: If you only have one evening, which one?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Tonight, De Materie, if you like contemporary opera. Tomorrow, eleven. And keep Les Misérables for a long Sunday afternoon.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That sounds like a plan. Honestly, I'd add Peter Grimes on the twenty-sixth to the diary now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good. Britten, a long wait, but worth marking.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A word about confidence. Low means we only have an interview or a synopsis. Medium means we read a review. High would mean a lot more, and we don't have it today.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right, and that is why we tell you whose opinion it is. We are not pretending to have seen the films.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. Pick your own, and tell us if we got it wrong.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, the idea of the day. A classic that plays it safe, a small Catalan horror film that might not, and a festival that is just beginning.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Cinema for every mood, then. The full edition has the sources and the details. Thanks for listening.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: See you tomorrow on the Radar.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: If you have a free evening this weekend, pick one of the three: the long classic, the small horror film, or the opera tonight.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And if you are curious about festivals, keep an eye on Tallinn. We'll report the awards when they come, on the twenty-second.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We'll also keep following the Royal Ballet and Opera's Carmen, to see whether it reaches a screen in Spain.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good. Enjoy the weekend, and enjoy the films.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Bye!
